sources.ref_file_title: LV15 - On Basing Private Information Retrieval on NP-Hardness
sources.note: Verified: TCC 2016-A pp. 372-386; ePrint 2015/1061 (Nov 2015). Scope confirmed: rules out reductions from SAT that use the PIR adversary as an oracle, ADAPTIVE queries allowed; consequence NP subset-of coAM.

pages.class_justification: LV15 rule out security reductions from SAT that make black-box use of the adversary breaking the PIR scheme; apart from being black-box in the adversary the reduction is unrestricted and may query adaptively. That is exactly RTV04's black-box-in-the-adversary shape, and since the hypothesis side is a complexity assumption rather than a primitive there is no construction component to weaken, so fully-black-box is the class ruled out. Recording `relativizing` would be an overstatement: LV15 give no oracle separation.
pages.model_justification: Standard model; barrier frontmatter carries no `model` field, so nothing to set.
pages.statement: A probabilistic polynomial-time reduction from $\mathrm{SAT}$ to breaking the privacy of a single-server, single-round [[single-server-private-information-retrieval|cPIR]] scheme, using the adversary only as an oracle, implies $\classNP \subseteq \classcoAM$ and hence a collapse of the [[polynomial-time-hierarchy|polynomial hierarchy]] to its second level. The reduction may query the adversary adaptively, and the result is tight in both the correctness and the privacy parameter of the scheme — [[LV15 - On Basing Private Information Retrieval on NP-Hardness|LV15]].
pages.sketch: Privacy of a single-round PIR scheme is broken given a $\classSZK$ oracle: deciding which index a query encodes is a statistical-difference problem. Substituting that oracle for the adversary in any reduction that uses the adversary as a black box places $\mathrm{SAT}$ in $\classcoAM$.
flags: no-np-to-cpir-lv15: consequence should become `kind: complexity, target: conp-subset-am` (NP subset-of coAM is equivalent to coNP subset-of AM, and schema/propositions.yaml already carries `conp-subset-am` with a note that the PH collapse is the downstream corollary, not the theorem). It is currently `kind: contradiction` with an empty target, which loses the theorem.

no-np-to-cpir-lv15: setting class to fully-black-box means the title becomes 'No fully-black-box reduction from NP to cPIR', per the convention on no-hash-function-to-pke-gkm-00 and no-ggm-to-dlog-sho97.

sources.authors: Adi Akavia, Oded Goldreich, Shafi Goldwasser, Dana Moshkovitz
sources.note: IMPORTANT: the paper's first result (arbitrary/adaptive reductions when |f^{-1}(y)| is efficiently computable) was RETRACTED by the authors in an erratum, STOC 2010 pp. 795-796, https://doi.org/10.1145/1806689.1806798 . Only the non-adaptive result stands.

sources.ref_file_title: BB15 - On Basing Size-Verifiable One-Way Functions on NP-Hardness
sources.note: Recovers, for size-verifiable one-way functions, the adaptive-reduction claim AGGM06 retracted: a general (adaptive) reduction of NP to inverting a size-verifiable OWF implies NP subset-of coAM. Also at https://www.iacr.org/archive/tcc2015/90140001/90140001.pdf and ECCC TR14-108. Likely cryptobib key TCC:BogBrz15 (verify before setting).

pages.class_justification: The result that survives is restricted to randomized NON-ADAPTIVE reductions, and RTV04's vocabulary has no slot for an adaptivity restriction. Recording `fully-black-box` would assert a barrier against adaptive black-box reductions of NP to inverting f, which AGGM06 explicitly retracted (erratum, STOC 2010) and which is known only for size-verifiable f (BB15). `unstated` is the honest value; the restriction is carried in the statement text instead.
pages.model_justification: Standard model; barrier frontmatter carries no `model` field.
pages.statement: For every polynomial-time computable $f$, a randomized non-adaptive reduction of $\classNP$ to the task of inverting $f$ on average implies $\classcoNP \subseteq \classAM$, and hence a collapse of the [[polynomial-time-hierarchy|polynomial hierarchy]] to its second level; the one-wayness of $f$ therefore cannot be based on worst-case $\classNP$-hardness by such a reduction — [[AGGM06 - On basing one-way functions on NP-hardness|AGGM06]].
pages.improvements_text:
- AGGM06's companion claim — that an arbitrary, adaptively querying reduction suffices whenever $|f^{-1}(y)|$ is efficiently computable — was retracted by the authors; only the non-adaptive result stands — [[AGGM06 - On basing one-way functions on NP-hardness|AGGM06]] erratum, STOC 2010.
- For *size-verifiable* one-way functions the adaptive case is recovered: a general reduction of $\classNP$ to inverting one implies $\classNP \subseteq \classcoAM$ — [[BB15 - On Basing Size-Verifiable One-Way Functions on NP-Hardness|BB15]].

sources.note: Existence verified (Cryptology ePrint Archive 2026/113, Feb 2026). Supplies the black-box construction of an OIHF from a random oracle and states that its OT construction is non-black-box precisely so as to evade the Impagliazzo-Rudich separation.

sources.note: Not an improvement - the underlying oracle separation that makes this barrier bite. Listed here only because the schema's `role` vocabulary has no slot for a co-source.

pages.class_justification: BH26 construct an OIHF from a random oracle by a black-box construction. Composing that with a hypothetical fully-black-box reduction from an OIHF to OT would yield a fully-black-box construction of OT (hence key agreement) from a random oracle, which IR89's oracle separation rules out. The barrier therefore rules out `fully-black-box`; this is exactly why BH26's own OT construction is non-black-box.
pages.model_justification: The barrier is about standard-model reductions; the random oracle enters only as the object BH26 build the OIHF from. Barrier frontmatter carries no `model` field.
pages.statement: An [[oblivious-interactive-hash-function|OIHF]] admits a black-box construction from a random oracle, so a fully-black-box reduction from an OIHF to [[oblivious-transfer|OT]] would compose into a fully-black-box construction of OT from a random oracle, contradicting the Impagliazzo–Rudich separation of key agreement from symmetric primitives — [[IR89 - Limits on the provable consequences of one-way permutations|IR89]]. BH26's construction of OT from an OIHF is accordingly non-black-box, and the Minicrypt/Cryptomania separation stands for black-box constructions — [[BH26 - How to Steal Oblivious Transfer from Minicrypt|BH26]].
notes_to_keep: This is a barrier-CIRCUMVENTION record: the IR89 Minicrypt/Cryptomania separation is partially bridged by a non-black-box reduction while the black-box separation stands. The data model has no edge type for 'circumvents barrier X by leaving class C'.

sources.note: Abstract stored on the wiki reference page matches: 'if P = NP, no protocol for secret key agreement is secure in such a setting ... as a corollary, there is an oracle relative to which the implication is false ... no technique which relativizes can prove that secret exchange can be based on any one-way permutation.'

sources.ref_file_title: BM09 - Merkle Puzzles Are Optimal An O(n2)-Query Attack on Any Key Exchange from a Random Oracle
sources.note: Tightens the eavesdropper's query complexity from IR89's ~O(n^6) to the optimal O(n^2).

pages.class_justification: IR89 exhibit an oracle — a random permutation together with a $\classPSPACE$-complete oracle, which forces $\classP = \classNP$ relative to it — under which one-way permutations exist but no key-agreement protocol is secure. An oracle separation rules out every relativizing reduction, and by the partial order in schema/reduction-classes.yaml that also kills every fully-black-box one. This is the worked example the schema file itself gives.
pages.model_justification: The separation is proved by an oracle argument but bars standard-model relativizing constructions; barrier frontmatter carries no `model` field.
pages.statement: There is an oracle relative to which [[one-way-permutation|one-way permutations]] exist but no [[key-exchange|key-agreement]] protocol is secure, so no relativizing — and in particular no fully-black-box — construction of key agreement from a one-way permutation exists. In its primary form the theorem is conditional: relative to a random permutation oracle, if $\classP = \classNP$ then every key-agreement protocol is broken, so proving any such construction secure is as hard as proving $\classP \neq \classNP$ — [[IR89 - Limits on the provable consequences of one-way permutations|IR89]].
pages.sketch: Relative to a random permutation $\pi$, an eavesdropper holding the transcript repeatedly samples executions of the two parties consistent with it and queries $\pi$ on every query that occurs with non-negligible probability; once she holds all queries the parties share, she can simulate one of them and recover the key. The sampling is not efficient in general but is if $\classP = \classNP$, which is what turns the attack into a barrier.
pages.security_loss: The eavesdropper makes $\tilde{O}(\ell^6)$ oracle queries against honest parties making $\ell$ queries; improved to the optimal $O(\ell^2)$ by BM09.
pages.improvements_text: - The eavesdropper's query complexity is optimally $O(\ell^2)$, matching Merkle's puzzles, so no random-oracle key agreement achieves a better-than-quadratic query gap — [[BM09 - Merkle Puzzles Are Optimal An O(n2)-Query Attack on Any Key Exchange from a Random Oracle|BM09]].
notes_to_keep: IR89's oracle is a random permutation together with a PSPACE-complete oracle; the migrated quotes omit the second oracle.

sources.note: Verified: 41st FOCS (2000), pp. 325-335. Abstract: 'Our main results show that public-key encryption and oblivious transfer are incomparable under black-box reductions ... Our techniques for showing negative results follow the oracle separations of R. Impagliazzo and S. Rudich (1989).'

pages.class_justification: GKM+00 state their negative results as showing PKE and OT incomparable under black-box reductions, proved by oracle separations in the style of IR89. That certainly rules out fully-black-box reductions. Whether their separation is a single fully relativizing oracle (which would rule out `relativizing` as well, a strictly broader claim under the partial order) is not settled by the abstract, so the narrower value is recorded.

pages.statement: There is no fully-black-box construction of [[oblivious-transfer|OT]] from [[public-key-encryption|PKE]]: the two primitives are incomparable under black-box reductions, by oracle separations in the style of Impagliazzo–Rudich. The separation is matched by positive results — a restricted, strengthened form of each primitive does imply the other — [[GKM+00 - The relationship between public key encryption and oblivious transfer|GKM+00]].

pages.class_justification: A communication lower bound in the random oracle model rules out every protocol in that model, not a proof technique, so it is the `free` class scoped by the model axis — the treatment schema/reduction-classes.yaml prescribes in its `generic-group` rejection message, and the one content/Barriers/no-ggm-to-dlog-sho97.md already uses for a Shoup-style generic lower bound.

pages.statement: Key agreement in the [[random-oracle-model|random oracle model]] cannot be made communication-efficient: for [[key-exchange|key-agreement]] protocols whose honest parties' oracle queries are uniformly random, or which run in two rounds with non-adaptive queries, secrecy against an eavesdropper making $O(\ell^2)$ queries requires the parties to exchange $\Omega(\ell)$ bits — the communication Merkle's puzzles already uses — [[HMO+19 - On the Communication Complexity of Key-Agreement Protocols|HMO+19]].
pages.sketch: For protocols whose honest queries are uniformly random the bound is proved by reduction from set-disjointness in two-party communication complexity; the two-round non-adaptive case is proved directly by an information-theoretic argument.
pages.improvements_text:
- Query complexity: every random-oracle key-agreement protocol whose honest parties make $\ell$ queries is broken by an eavesdropper making $O(\ell^2)$ queries, matching Merkle's puzzles — [[BM09 - Merkle Puzzles Are Optimal An O(n2)-Query Attack on Any Key Exchange from a Random Oracle|BM09]].
- The original random-oracle barrier, with an $\tilde{O}(\ell^6)$-query eavesdropper — [[IR89 - Limits on the provable consequences of one-way permutations|IR89]].
flags: HIGH PRIORITY no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19: `strength` must change from `unconditional` to `conditional`, with `conditional-on: [honest parties' oracle queries are uniformly random, or the protocol is two-round with non-adaptive queries]`. HMO+19's bound holds only under those structural restrictions - they are exactly what makes the result conditional, and dropping them turns a true theorem into a false one.

HIGH PRIORITY no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19: the bare hyperedge {rom} => ke barred is FALSE without a quantitative qualifier - Merkle's puzzles IS a random-oracle key-agreement protocol (Mer78). Every result on this page is a quantitative bound (query gap, communication), so the qualifier is load-bearing and must survive into the statement or the page asserts something untrue.

no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19: the page bundles three results. BM09's optimality theorem is the subject of the sibling page no-rom-to-merkle-puzzles-bm09 (which I flag as wrong_claim); once that page is retyped to conclusion `ke` the two collide on one hyperedge and must be reconciled - suggested split is no-rom-to-ke-bm09 (query gap) and no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19 (communication).

HIGH PRIORITY no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19: CONFIRMED MATH ERRORS on content/Primitives/key-exchange.md. 'Any KE protocol from a random oracle requires Omega(n) queries' is not a BM09 result and is vacuous as written; 'Merkle puzzles achieve O(n^2) security' inverts the quantity. BM09's theorem is an UPPER bound on the ATTACKER: any n-query protocol is broken by an O(n^2)-query eavesdropper. The same page calls HMO+19 'information-theoretic key agreement', which misnames the model (random oracle with query-bounded parties). Skeptical-checker lane.

no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19: content/References/BM09 ... .md line 19 says BM09 improves 'the Omega(n^6)-query lower bound of IR89'. BM09's own abstract says it improves the previous ~O(n^6)-query ATTACK of Impagliazzo-Rudich - an upper bound on the eavesdropper, not a lower bound. Both wordings appear on the wiki and disagree.

no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19: dead wikilink `[[Mer78]]` inside the migrated quote (the reference page exists as 'Mer78 - Secure Communications Over Insecure Channels'); already tracked in TODO_SUMMARY.md:20 and bot_flagged in .fact-check/queue.json.

no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19: content/Glossary/black-box-separations.md closes this passage with 'Together, IR89 and BM09 give a complete picture of the complexity of key agreement in the random oracle model' - a recap paragraph CLAUDE.md forbids, and false given the same page cites HMO+19 as an open strand on communication complexity.

no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19: key says 19 but the venue is ITCS 2021 (arXiv:2105.01958). The wiki key wins per the instructions; noted for the reference-fixer, and `npm run sync-cryptobib` against ITCS:HMORY19 may flag the `venue`/`published` fields.

pages.wrong_reason: The conclusion object is a construction, not a primitive, and the edge points the wrong way. Merkle's puzzles IS a key-agreement protocol in the random oracle model - Mer78 builds it - so {rom} => merkle-puzzles is a positive construction that exists, and a barrier ruling it out is false. What BM09 prove is a quantitative optimality bound on a different hyperedge, {rom} => ke: every random-oracle key-agreement protocol whose honest parties make at most $n$ oracle queries is broken by an eavesdropper making $O(n^2)$ queries, so no random-oracle key agreement achieves a better-than-quadratic query gap. Retype with conclusion `ke`, class `free`, model rom (following content/Barriers/no-ggm-to-dlog-sho97.md), carrying the better-than-quadratic qualifier in the statement - at which point it is the BM09 strand currently bundled into bar-rom-to-ke-hmo-19 and the two must be reconciled, e.g. as no-rom-to-ke-bm09 (query gap) alongside no-rom-to-ke-hmo-19 (communication).
